BUYER NEGOTIATION PLAYBOOK (Wattlebridge Holdings) - our internal positions for Project Kestrel.
Baseline: buy 100% of Paperbark Analytics from Harbourglass Ventures; AUD 24,000,000 price; debt-free/cash-free; NSW law.

- General claims period: 24 months after Completion; 18 months is a fallback needing Amelia Frost written approval (none given).
- Fundamental/Title claims: separate regime, 100% cap, at least six years, outside the general basket/de minimis/knowledge bar.

From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from our playbook, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel: Seller Draft Review Against Buyer Playbook

**Status note:** The Seller's document is a counterparty proposal. It calls its positions "key negotiated" and "fair and balanced," but nothing in it is agreed or cleared. Several of its numbers match our fallback positions, but none of those fallbacks has the required authority: no written approval from Amelia Frost has been given for any of them. The disclosure facts are also dated to 22 September 2026, about six weeks ago, so they need refreshing before we rely on them.

## 1. Departure Matrix

| Issue | Seller position | Playbook position | Gap |
|---|---|---|---|
| General cap (12.1) | 20% / AUD 4.8m | Start 25% / AUD 6.0m. 20% only as a conditional fallback with Amelia Frost's written authority | Starts at our fallback without authority. Reject |
| De minimis (12.2) | AUD 25,000 | AUD 5,000 | 5x our threshold. Reject |
| Basket (12.2) | AUD 250,000, excess-only recovery | AUD 50,000 aggregate, first-dollar once exceeded | 5x basket and deductible-style recovery. Reject |
| General claims period (12.3/13) | 18 months | 24 months (18 months only with Amelia Frost approval) | Reject |
| Limitation spillover (12.3/13) | Any claim limit applies to all claims unless excluded | Keep categories separate; no hidden general-regime override | Reject |
| Fundamental/Title | Same caps and time limits as general | 100% cap, at least 6 years, outside basket/de minimis/knowledge bar | Directly contrary. Reject |
| Limitations/reliance (9.3/12.8/20.5) | Apply to all claims of any nature | Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of everything | No carve-out offered. Reject |
| Disclosure (Sch 7, 1.1, 1.2) | Whole data room, accounts, statutory registers, public records | Specific fair disclosure only; reject deemed disclosure | Reject |
| Buyer knowledge (8.3) | Bars claims for anything known or discoverable from data room or public records | Delete blanket exclusions; named seller knowledge persons plus reasonable enquiry; never excuse title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities | Reject |
| Bluefen (3/6.3) | Reasonable endeavours; satisfied on delivery of consent | Effective consent AND evidence conditions satisfied before Completion | Reject. Consent-on-delivery and endeavours alone are insufficient |
| Riverlark (2/7) | Release after Completion | Current payout, direct repayment from Completion funds, effective releases; post-completion release only with irrevocable undertaking and Amelia Frost approval | Reject |
| Employee bonuses / funds flow | Not itemised; "a matter for the Seller" | AUD 420,000 plus on-costs as a specific line item or seller-funded | Reject |
| Ironquay IP (11.1) | Indemnity limited to SOW3 payment; "adequate" | Broaden the indemnity; preserve SOW3 cure; AUD 180,000 unverified | Reject as drafted |
| DD-006 export incident (4.6/Sch 6) | "Not expected to be material" | No conclusion either way; preserve logs, investigate, require updates | Reject characterisation |
| Sandbar renewals | "Ordinary-course operating costs" | Assess; no automatic Debt classification or price deduction | Assess before accepting the characterisation |
| Tax / IP | "Settled under the general regime" | OPEN; no unlimited liability and no resolution | Reject |
| Title (DD-012) | Share register evidences title | Independent title, ownership, encumbrance and authority evidence required | Reject. The register is an internal source |

## 2. Material Issues and Reasoning

**(a) Caps, thresholds and time limits (12.1 to 13).** Every general-regime number is worse than our starting position, and the 20% cap, 18-month period and the existence of a basket are all fallbacks that have not been authorised. The Seller's "limitation applies to all Claims" clause is the most dangerous drafting point. Combined with its fundamental-claims proposal, it would pull title and capacity claims into the general regime, which would cap and time-limit our most important protections.

**(b) Fundamental and title claims.** The Seller's "administrative simplicity" rationale does not justify limiting title and capacity protection. Title is what we are buying. Those warranties need their own regime at 100% and at least six years, outside the basket, de minimis and knowledge bar.

**(c) Fraud carve-out.** The reliance and exclusive-remedy provisions apply to "all Claims of any nature," and no fraud carve-out is offered. This must be added to every cap, basket, time limit, exclusive remedy and non-reliance provision, to the maximum extent enforceable. No one can waive it.

**(d) Disclosure and buyer knowledge.** Disclosure 1.1 and 1.2 deem the whole data room, accounts and public registers disclosed. Clause 8.3 then bars claims for anything "discoverable" from those sources. Together they would make Wattlebridge bear the risk of every document in a 2026 data room, and would effectively gut the warranty package. Reject both, require specific disclosure, and limit any knowledge qualifier to named seller persons after reasonable enquiry. Knowledge should never excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.

**(e) Bluefen (about AUD 3.6m, around 30% of revenue per DD-002).** The Seller's own disclosure (item 2) confirms that no final written consent and no evidence of satisfied conditions is included. The proposed "consent on delivery" and reasonable-endeavours standard would let the sale complete without the key customer's consent. Consent and evidence of satisfied conditions should be Completion conditions, not post-signing obligations.

**(f) Riverlark (about AUD 3.2m).** The disclosure confirms the facility has not been repaid and no discharge is included. Deferring the release to after Completion leaves the company's assets encumbered and our exposure open. Repayment should come directly from Completion funds, with releases delivered at Completion. Any post-Completion release needs an irrevocable undertaking and Amelia Frost's approval.

**(g) Funds flow and bonuses (AUD 420,000).** The bonuses are conditional, not contingent on nothing, and the funds flow is silent on them. The disclosure does not say whether payroll tax or superannuation applies, so the on-cost quantum is unknown. Either the bonuses appear as a specific line item with on-costs, or the Seller funds them. We should not accept a funds flow that quietly leaves them out.

**(h) Ironquay (AUD 180,000 open).** Clause 7.3 of DD-004 conditions transfer of SOW3 materials on payment, and the disclosure confirms no receipt or confirmatory assignment exists. The Seller's indemnity covers only the SOW3 payment, which is too narrow. It should be broadened to cover the wider Ironquay IP position and must preserve the SOW3 cure. The AUD 180,000 figure is not independently verified either way, so we should verify it with bank or invoice evidence rather than accept or reject it on the figure alone.

**(i) DD-006 export/privacy incident.** The Seller says the matter is "not expected to be material." That is a conclusion the material does not support. The disclosure itself says it is preliminary, does not establish access, scope or notification requirements, and states no loss amount. We should assume no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand in either direction. In practice that means: preserve logs, require the investigation to be completed with regular written updates, and reserve our position on any specific indemnity for consequences of the incident. We should not adopt the Seller's materiality view.

**(j) Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000).** Three renewals at AUD 110,000 each are described as "ordinary-course," but the disclosure says it does not state whether they are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course. We need to assess them. We should not automatically classify them as Debt or deduct them from price.

**(k) Tax and IP.** The Seller says these are "settled under the general regime." They are not settled. Our playbook keeps them open, with no unlimited liability and no resolution, and requires them to sit in their own categories rather than under the general regime.

**(l) Title (DD-012).** The Seller relies on its own company share register. That is an internal source, not independent proof. We need independent evidence of title, ownership, encumbrances and authority before Completion.

**(m) Items not covered by the playbook.** The office lease (DD-007, notification obligation, no landlord consent stated) and Mossvale (DD-009, assignment restriction, no consent stated) have no playbook position. The team should confirm whether either needs a consent check or a condition before we rely on the Seller's silence.

## 3. Recommendations

1. **Reject the Seller's package as drafted** and send a mark-up that restates our starting positions. Do not offer the 20% cap, 18-month period, or any other fallback without Amelia Frost's written authority identifying the draft.
2. **Reset the general regime:** 25% / AUD 6.0m cap, AUD 5,000 de minimis, AUD 50,000 first-dollar basket, 24-month period.
3. **Separate the fundamental/title regime:** 100% cap, at least six years, outside the basket, de minimis and knowledge bar. Strike the "same caps and time limits" proposal.
4. **Add the fraud carve-out** to all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable.
5. **Replace disclosure:** strike whole-data-room, accounts, register and public-record deemed disclosure. Require specific fair disclosure.
6. **Delete blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion (8.3).** Any qualifier needs named seller knowledge persons and reasonable enquiry, and never excuses title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities.
7. **Bluefen:** make effective consent and evidence of satisfied conditions a pre-Completion condition. Reject consent-on-delivery and reasonable-endeavours-only drafting.
8. **Riverlark:** require a current payout letter, direct repayment from Completion funds, and effective security releases at Completion. Any post-Completion release needs an irrevocable undertaking and Amelia Frost's approval.
9. **Bonuses:** require the AUD 420,000 plus on-costs as a specific funds-flow line item or Seller-funded. Get a payroll tax and superannuation view.
10. **Ironquay:** broaden the indemnity beyond SOW3, preserve the SOW3 cure, and verify the AUD 180,000 with bank or invoice evidence.
11. **DD-006:** preserve logs, require the investigation and regular written updates, and reserve our position on a specific indemnity. Reject the "not material" characterisation.
12. **Sandbar:** assess the three renewals on their terms. No automatic Debt classification or price deduction.
13. **Tax and IP:** keep open, in separate categories, with no unlimited liability and no general-regime override.
14. **Title:** require independent evidence of title, ownership, encumbrances and authority. Treat DD-012 as an internal source only.
15. **Refresh the facts:** update all disclosure items from the 22 September 2026 cut-off to current, and confirm the status of the office lease and Mossvale items.
16. **Escalate to Amelia Frost** for any decision on the fallback positions. No fallback is currently authorised.
